headline: Android App Development Cost in 2026: Ranges, Drivers and How to Estimate
description: What an Android app costs to build in 2026: indicative ranges for an MVP and a market-ready app, what Android-only really saves, and how to estimate your own.

itemListElement.name: Android App Development Cost in 2026: Ranges, Drivers and How to Estimate

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to build an Android app in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Using our method, a lean Android MVP is about 6 weeks and roughly $11k to $19k, and a market-ready Android app with payments, an admin dashboard and a custom backend is about 22 weeks and roughly $40k to $70k. These are indicative ranges.

mainEntity.name: Is it cheaper to build only for Android?

acceptedAnswer.text: Slightly. In our model a single platform is about 10 percent less than building both from one shared codebase, because most of the work is shared.

mainEntity.name: Should I build native Android or cross-platform?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choose native when the app relies on Android-specific capabilities. For most business apps a cross-platform codebase is more economical and makes adding iOS later straightforward.

mainEntity.name: What makes Android apps more expensive to test?

acceptedAnswer.text: The range of devices, screen sizes and OS versions. Supporting older and lower-end phones adds testing and performance work.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build an Android app?

acceptedAnswer.text: About 6 weeks for a lean MVP and about 22 weeks for a market-ready product in our examples, depending on features, backend and design.
